cards.back: Retrieve relevant external information, then generate using that context—retrieve-then-generate.
Data grows faster than limits; long context ≠ good use of context; RAG picks query-specific, cost-controlled chunks.
Retriever quality—bad retrieval cannot be fully fixed by a strong generator.
Sparse: term/BM25-style overlap. Dense: embedding similarity. Hybrid often wins in production.
System that plans and acts—often with tools—beyond a single retrieve-then-answer turn.

cards.front: Shared requirement for RAG and agents?
cards.back: Rigorous evaluation and security (prompt injection via retrieved/tool content).
